output.reason: A 68-year-old with COPD reporting two days of worsening dyspnea now provoked by walking to the bathroom plus green phlegm needs hands-on assessment today with oxygen saturation, lung exam and chest imaging, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — urgent care or ED — for an oxygen-level check, lung exam and chest X-ray, since your breathlessness now happens just walking to the bathroom and your phlegm changed color. Call 911 right away if you struggle to speak in full sentences, feel confused or drowsy, your lips turn blue, or you have chest pain.
differential: Pneumonia or other complication (e.g. heart failure, PE) causing worsening dyspnea

redFlags.concern: Dyspnea at minimal exertion, worse than baseline
redFlags.quote: now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom

output.vitalSigns: No oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate or temperature reported; whether any measurement was taken is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Severity cannot be graded remotely without oxygen saturation, work-of-breathing assessment or imaging.

citations.quote: **Definition:** Acute sustained worsening of dyspnea, cough, and/or sputum (volume or purulence) beyond normal day-to-day variation, requiring a change in therapy.
citations.claim: Sustained worsening of dyspnea and sputum purulence beyond normal variation defines an acute COPD exacerbation requiring a change in therapy.
citations.limitation: Definition only; severity class not established without examination or oxygen measurement.

citations.quote: ** Pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, and acute heart failure all cause dyspnea and wheezing in COPD patients.
citations.claim: Pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism and heart failure also cause dyspnea in COPD patients, so chest imaging is advised rather than assuming COPD alone.
citations.limitation: Emergency-department reference; wheezing and exam findings are not reported for this patient.

Do not invent an inhaler or rescue regimen; a prescription/plan mention alone is not authority for a new instruction. Targeted prose finding, not prescribing validation.
Do not ask the patient to palpate or probe a wound for bone; that examination belongs to a trained clinician.
Reported wakefulness cannot establish absence of loss of consciousness or neurological injury; targeted observed-error check.
Absence of surgery/trauma alone does not exclude spontaneous CSF leakage; limited causal-phrase regression, not full reasoning verification.
Do not import routine nosebleed positioning into suspected penetrating head injury; follow dispatcher instructions. Targeted regression.
Worsening and ten-day persistence are separate reasons to seek care; targeted observed-wording check.

applicationAudit.limitation: No finding is not a pass. Patient text is identity-bound, not generally semantically parsed. Reported diagnoses/examinations do not acquire independent verification. Only enumerated applications associated with cited, contracted sources are inspected; other paraphrases, uncited sources and arbitrary prose remain unassessed. The red-flag check covers only impairment denial from mixed functioning-but-tired/sleepy/exhausted quotations without an explicit negative cue. No Ottawa exclusion rule is activated without an established source witness.
